notes:
Charcoal is produced by pyrolysis (heating wood in the absence of oxygen) — modeled via the vanilla Smelter 2.5 m, same pattern as Stone & Concrete reusing the Smelter as a kiln. Fruits and resin are renewable byproducts of the Arboretum 5 m; they exist primarily as forward-hooks to future Food and Plastics mods (no consumer in v0.1, but machine-discoverable via their `producedBy` strings). Wood ash forward-references Stone & Concrete's Cement, mirroring the coal-ash pattern.

Energy math: wood direct burn 6 kW × 27s = 162 kJ/unit; charcoal 18 kW × 30s = 540 kJ/unit; refining ratio 2 wood → 1 charcoal gives 324 kJ direct vs 540 kJ refined → +67% energy recovery, matching real-world charcoal economics.

resources.description: Carbonized wood produced by pyrolysis in the Smelter 2.5 m. Chemically similar to anthracite coal — burns cleanly in Coal Power's Combustion Generator 2.5 m at ~40% efficiency (matching coal briquette performance). Two wood yield one charcoal: the mass loss is water and volatiles driven off during pyrolysis.

Edible plant produce — apples, berries, and stone fruits growing on mature trees. Produced renewably by the Arboretum 5 m alongside wood and resin. Forward-looking: a future Food mod can consume fruits directly (raw ration) or as an ingredient in prepared-food recipes. In v0.1 this is a declarative hook only — no Food mod exists yet.
resources.producedBy: Arboretum 5 m (renewable byproduct of tree cultivation)

resources.description: Viscous tree sap harvested from mature trees. Real-world feedstock for bio-plastics (polylactic acid analogues), varnishes, and adhesives. Produced renewably by the Arboretum 5 m alongside wood and fruits. Forward-looking: a future Plastics mod can consume resin as the bio-plastic feedstock pathway (alongside petroleum-derived naphtha as the petro-plastic pathway). In v0.1 this is a declarative hook only — no Plastics mod exists yet.
resources.producedBy: Arboretum 5 m (renewable byproduct of tree cultivation)

resources.description: Fine mineral residue left after wood or charcoal is consumed in Coal Power's Combustion Generator 2.5 m. Real-world wood ash is a supplementary cementitious material (mildly pozzolanic — not as strong as fly ash from coal but still usable). Forward-looking: a future revision of Stone & Concrete's Cement recipe can optionally accept wood ash alongside coal ash and stone powder. In v0.1 this is metadata only; Stone & Concrete is unchanged.
resources.producedBy: Combustion Generator 2.5 m (byproduct of burning wood or charcoal)
